task.note: Apple's own sv for Task (iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime: System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/WorkflowKit.framework | Localizable.strings | Task (Parameter Label), sv 'Uppgift'; System/Library/Frameworks/ClassKit.framework | ClassKit.strings | CONTEXT_TYPE_TASK, sv 'Uppgift'). 'aktivitet' is the loan a translator reaches for and is never right here; it does collide with a real Swedish sense — Apple's own Screen Time access alert says '...kan den se dina aktivitetsdata...' (NOTIFICATION_AUTH_REQUEST_MESSAGE_INDIVIDUAL), so 'aktivitetsdata' is the Swedish phrase for Screen Time's own activity data. That collision happens to fall outside this concept's own key list, so no term_audit conflict results from it, but 'aktivitet' stays forbidden here regardless, because the app's task concept and Screen Time's activity data must not share a word even where the two never render on the same key.

restricted_list.note: The named set of apps and categories blocked during a session (screenTime.createRestrictedList.*, screenTime.restrictedAppsPicker.*, plan.createToDo.removeRestrictedApps, plan.createToDo.restrictedAppsSection, focusTask.createTask.restrictedAppsSectionTitle). Chosen as one closed compound, matching Swedish's ban on splitting compounds across two words: 'blockering' is what happens to the apps, plain and accurate. forbidden marks the blacklist calque the concept note rules out ('blacklist' is explicitly not this concept); it cannot catch a paraphrase such as 'lista över blockerade appar', which is drift for the editor to report.

time_value.note: Focused time priced at the user's own rate, shown as money and never received (insights.savings.*, achievements.category.wages.*, widgets.cash.*, widgets.monthlyTimeValue.*, widgets.focusRing.a11y.money, onboarding.with*Moneyfesting.*). 'värde' is Apple's own sv for Value (iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime: System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/HealthRecordsUI.framework | HealthRecordsUI-Localizable.strings | MEDICAL_RECORD_DETAIL_TITLE_VALUE, sv 'Värde'). forms lists the closed compound in the cases the labels need; a paraphrase the batch may coin ('värdet av din tid') is drift, not a form, and the editor should flag it toward the compound instead. forbidden holds the two outcome nouns nearest to this concept ('inkomst'/income, 'vinst'/profit); whole-word matching means these do not hit unrelated compounds, but a plain grep for the stem will, which the brief's Money frame records.

time_value_disclaimer.note: The fixed sentence after a time-value figure, on 11 en keys (achievements.badge.*.earned (7), achievements.category.wages.description, widgets.cash.description, widgets.focusRing.a11y.money, widgets.monthlyTimeValue.description). hourly_rate.note: The rate the user sets to price their own time (onboarding.hourlyWage.*, profile.hourlyWage.*, currency.settings.*, screenTimeReport.missingWage, achievements.category.wages.description). 'pris' is Apple's own sv for Price (iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime: System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/StoreKitUI.framework | Gifting.strings | GIFTING_CONFIRM_PRICE_LABEL, sv 'Pris'). 'timlön' is correct Swedish for an hourly wage and exactly the wrong word here, because the app pays nobody; en says 'hourly wage' on several keys, so a translator will reach for it, which is why it is forbidden rather than merely discouraged. The badge names in the payroll family may use employment vocabulary ('månadsavlönad' for the Salaried badge); running copy pricing the user's own time may not use 'lön' or its compounds.

daily_focus_goal.note: The daily minutes target drawn as a ring, met or not met (onboarding.dailyFocusGoal.*, profile.focusTarget.*, widgets.focusRing.*). Closed compound of 'dag' + 'mål', matching Swedish's ban on splitting compounds. forbidden is empty on purpose: the words a wrong draft would use ('syfte', 'ambition') are correct everyday Swedish that onboarding.personalGoal.* and the quote surfaces may legitimately need for an aspiration, so banning them would fire on correct copy.

minute_unit.note: The compact minute unit, spaced by default and glued only on a render verdict (common.durationMinuteUnit, insights.sessions.durationMinuteUnit, share.duration.minutesShort and minutesOnly, screenTimeReport.durationMinutesOnly, widgets.streak.focusedInStreak, widgets.streak.focusedMinutesSummary, moneyfesting.details.timeElapsedFormat, component.templateTaskCard.duration). Foundation's sv_SE narrow duration form prints '1 h 45 m' and '25 m' with U+202F before the unit; the abbreviated report form spells minutes 'min' with a comma before the hour unit ('1 tim, 45 min'). forbidden is empty because the drift form is the single letter 'm' left over from en, which collides with the metre abbreviation in general Swedish and is an editor finding, recorded in the brief's Short forms table instead.

screen_time.note: Apple's sv name for the feature (iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime: Applications/Preferences.app | Localizable.strings | Screen Time, sv 'Skärmtid'; System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/ScreenTimeSettingsUI.framework | Localizable.strings | ScreenTimeControllerTitle), on the 18 en keys that name it. What this list cannot cover: Swedish uses the same word for the generic notion of time spent on a screen, and term_audit matches case-insensitively, so a count here mixes the feature (capital S, e.g. insights.appUsage.title) with the generic sense (lower case, e.g. screenTimeReport.noData, insights.savings.estimateExplanation). Only the English name is forbidden; the case distinction is drift for the editor to report, not a forbidden form, because lower-case 'skärmtid' is ordinary Swedish elsewhere.

forecast.note: The month-end projection of time value (insights.savings.forecast, insights.savings.*EstimateExplanation, insights.appUsage.permissionDescription, widgets.monthlyTimeValue.*). Swedish keeps this apart from the month-end figure without effort: 'prognos' is the forecast and 'uppskattning' the estimate (insights.savings.monthEnd, insights.savings.estimated), so this stays two words the way the ro brief's open forecast decision never quite settles. VoiceOver reads the two one after the other, so they must stay two words. forbidden marks the two nouns that would turn an estimate into a claim; 'garanti' is also a banned outcome word in the brief's Money frame.

open.recommended_reason: It is the shortest option that unambiguously means an unbroken run on its own, established in Swedish sports writing, and it compounds cleanly for a widget header.
open.note: No sv copy exists, so all three counts are 0. Keys: widgets.streak.* (39 keys at this snapshot), share.card.streak*, streakFreeze.* (11), paywall.benefit.streak.*, onboarding.welcome.slide.streak.*, insights.summary.dayStreakTitle, achievements.streak.*. Evidence per option: 'svit' is the established Swedish sports-writing word for an unbroken run ('en vinstsvit på fem matcher') and gives 'DAGSVIT' for the DAY STREAK caption; 'räcka' is the more literary word for a run or series, correct but less at home in consumer/sports copy; 'streak' is an English gaming/betting loanword, understood but not Apple's own style anywhere harvested. Apple's own Fitness translations never use a bare noun for this concept at all, always the periphrasis 'X dagar i följd' (iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime: System/Library/Health/Assets/FitnessUIAssets.bundle/ActivityAchievements/365AllGoals/localization | Localizable.stringsdict | ACHIEVEMENT_UNACHIEVED_PROGRESS_THREE_AWAY_DESC/NSStringLocalizedFormatKey), which supports the plain fallback for body copy but does not answer what a compact widget header needs on its own. Meanwhile agents write the days instead of the noun ('%lld dagar i följd'), never pick per string, and the adjudicator lists every key that touched the concept; nothing enters glossary/sv.json terms until the owner closes this. Decide before the first sv batch; a flip afterwards is a global term change with its own follow-up batch.

Evidence per option: '-pass' is the standard Swedish suffix for a timed activity segment (no single Apple citation needed; it is ordinary Swedish word formation); 'fokussession' matches Apple's own unchanged borrowing of 'Session' (iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime: System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/SensorKitUI.framework/AuthGroups/ECG.bundle | InfoPlist.strings | Session, sv 'Session' unchanged) but reads more clinical; 'koncentrationspass' is longer for no clear gain. open.recommended_reason: The suffix sits directly against a money figure the money frame already asks readers to read carefully, and the app's 'k' shares nothing with the locale's own thousands token 'tn', unlike the millions pair which at least shares an initial letter.
open.note: An engineering finding, not a copy choice, recorded here because agents meet it in packets. AppCurrency.formatCompact appends a hardcoded Latin 'k', 'm' or 'b' (Manifesting/Foundation/Localization/AppCurrency.swift:53-56), so sv renders '1,25k SEK', '1,25m SEK' and '1,25b SEK', while sv_SE's own compact tokens from Foundation's Decimal.FormatStyle.Currency(...).notation(.compactName) are 'tn' (thousand), 'mn' (million) and 'md' (billion): '1,25 tn SEK', '1,25 mn SEK', '1,25 md SEK'. Severity is medium: millions share an initial letter ('m' vs 'mn') but thousands ('k' vs 'tn') and billions ('b' vs 'md') do not, so a reader could misjudge the size of the figure — the billion case shares no letters at all, at least as severe as the thousands mismatch. Surfaces: widgets.focusRing.row.money, widgets.monthlyTimeValue.*, insights.savings.*, screenTimeReport.*, and the insights, celebration and session screens. Using the locale's notation changes the formatter for every locale, not just sv. Meanwhile agents never translate around the suffix, never spell it into copy, and report it once per batch that renders a compact amount; accessibility labels use the full format and are unaffected.
